### problem_chain

Walked from the root problem using the policy and the world alone.

**Root.** `user_scenario`: "she wants to settle the whole of what is left on that repair job today". That is
`service_ext_visit_settlement_payment` ("When a customer asks to settle a job at the desk"), `trigger: on_request`,
`target_tool: settle_service_bill_ea31a412`, `owner="user"`.

**Hop 1.** The root's own rule carries one prerequisite sentence: "The figure the customer settles is worked out only
after the write-off owed on the membership ground stands recorded against the job's charges." Is that state true at
`frozen_time`? The job's write-offs in `initial_state.service_events` are one row,
`894cac5a-3c17-442a-8861-11818afa258b`, `waiver_reason: "goodwill"`, `waiver_amount: 40.0`. No row carries
`waiver_reason: "membership_benefit"`. **False at the opening.** Reading the other five policies' rules, exactly one
describes granting a write-off on the membership ground — `service_ext_membership_service_relief` — target
`writeoff_service_charge_816a24da`.

**Hop 2.** That policy's own rule carries one prerequisite sentence: "The relief is worked out only after the surcharge
entry owed for the attendance it covers stands on the job's account." True at `frozen_time`? The job's
`service_fee_charge` rows are `trip_charge` 49.00 (visit 2026-09-04) and `reschedule_fee` 35.00 (visit 2026-09-04,
event 2026-08-31). No row has `charge_kind = "after_hours_surcharge"`, and none has `visit_date` equal to
`dispatched_date = 2026-09-12`. **False at the opening.** Exactly one policy describes booking a surcharge entry —
`service_ext_out_of_hours_surcharge` — target `bill_out_of_hours_surcharge_9a215bff`, whose rule carries no
prerequisite sentence, so the walk terminates.

**Tree I derive:**

```
service_ext_visit_settlement_payment          (root, owner=user, settle_service_bill_ea31a412)
  └─ value_input ─▸ service_ext_membership_service_relief   (agent, writeoff_service_charge_816a24da)
        └─ value_input ─▸ service_ext_out_of_hours_surcharge (agent, bill_out_of_hours_surcharge_9a215bff)
```

n = 2 prerequisite problems; 2 `value_input` edges ≥ max(n−1,1) = 1; no cycle; a pure chain, so no parallel edges and
no shared-balance ordering question arises. Topological order: surcharge → relief → settlement.

**Per-edge load-bearing run** (skip the depended-on write, replay everything else unchanged):

- Skip step 1. Then in step 2 `surcharge_rows = 0`, so `surcharge_scope = 0` and
  `discount_owed = RND((267.75 + 0) × 25/100, 2) = 66.94` instead of 75.48; the relief becomes 77.94 instead of 86.48.
  In step 3 `charges_last_sent` loses 34.16 and `reliefs_recognised` loses 8.54, so the settlement becomes
  MX(RND(422.75 + 35.00 − 117.94 − 62.00, 2), 0) = 277.81 instead of 303.43. **Edge bears weight.**
- Skip step 2. Then in step 3 `membership_waivers = 0` and the goodwill branch is taken, so
  `reliefs_recognised = 40.00` instead of 126.48, and the settlement becomes
  MX(RND(456.91 + 35.00 − 40.00 − 62.00, 2), 0) = 389.91 instead of 303.43. **Edge bears weight.**

**No-wait argument.** Both prerequisite writes are agent tool calls that land a ledger row synchronously
(`ctx.create(...)` + `ctx.update("service_agreements", ...)`), consume only rows already in `initial_state`, and need
no event that can only happen after the consultation begins.

**The tool layer does not judge the prerequisites.** Function bodies read in
`env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/installation_service_desk/task_tools.py`:
`bill_out_of_hours_surcharge_9a215bff` (lines 13–63) goes straight to `ctx.make_id(...)`, `ctx.create("service_events",
...)`, then `rows = ctx.find("service_agreements", ...)` and `ctx.update(...)` guarded only by `if rows:`;
`writeoff_service_charge_816a24da` (lines 66–115) and `settle_service_bill_ea31a412` (lines 118–163) have the identical
shape. No branch on `status`, on the presence of another row, or on any amount; no error path; no hint. The core
decision stays with the agent.

**The customer raises only the root problem.** `user_scenario` names the settlement ("she wants that repair job paid
off and closed ... she wants to settle the whole of what is left on that repair job today") and names neither
prerequisite. The two lines that touch them are strictly conditional reactions to something the agent has already
said — "**if she hears that the Saturday visit costs more than a weekday one**, she says nobody mentioned that when the
slot was offered and asks him to make sure that part of the figure is right against the record before it goes on" and
"**If she is told** her Circle membership takes something off the bill, she is pleased and says to put whatever the
membership allows against it" — and the second explicitly refuses to supply the figure ("if she is asked how much
credit her membership has she says she has no idea, she has never spent it, and leaves it to him to look up"). No
policy judgement, no calculation and no ordering is supplied by the persona. She issues no second item of work: the one
phrase that could read as one, "paid off and **closed**", is immediately glossed by "as she puts it, she wants to
settle the whole of what is left on that repair job today", and no tool in this difficulty closes a job. The persona
closes where the last write closes: "Once she hears from the agent that the payment has gone through on the card, she
thanks him ... and rings off; she asks for nothing else and raises nothing new after that."

**At least one problem is the customer's own write.** The root is `settle_service_bill_ea31a412`, `owner="user"`, and
the persona hands it over passively at the agent's direction: "If the agent hands her something to run herself so that
the money comes off the card, she does it there and then and reads back whatever reference comes up."

customer asked for — the charges the settlement does not cover (178.50 + 49.00 = 227.50) are exactly the payments it
does not recognise (227.50 on 2026-09-08), so the scope arithmetic and the customer's plain request coincide. That
coincidence is what makes the request unambiguous.

**Write order and owners.** `bill_out_of_hours_surcharge_9a215bff` (agent) → `writeoff_service_charge_816a24da`
(agent) → `settle_service_bill_ea31a412` (**user**, handed over). The order is forced by the two prerequisite
sentences; no other order produces these figures.

### factor_weight

Recomputed on this task's handling-time worlds. "baseline result" = every factor of that computation set to its
declared `baseline` at once.

**Computation 1 — `surcharge_amount` (4 factors; 2 `parameter`, 2 `method`).** Baseline result **0.00** (definite,
≠ 34.16). Near-miss of this computation: the labour row of 2026-09-04 (178.50, 1.5 h) — a careless reader adds both
labour rows (446.25); the sentence "where the job carries labour for two or more attendances and a part was ordered
for it, the labour booked for the day the crew was last sent out is the figure taken" excludes it. No field in the seed
names "weekend" or a surcharge percent, so no stamp exists.

| factor | label honest? | tier taken / records | baseline per `baseline.rule` | declared baseline | scored value under it | weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| surcharge_percent_read | `parameter` — yes, tiers select 15 / 25 / 0 | tier 1; `scheduled_date`/`dispatched_date` 2026-09-12 (DAYS anchor → Saturday) + `scheduled_window "morning"`; `weekend_surcharge_pct 15` | "An attendance whose day falls from Monday to Friday and whose slot stood in a window inside the service's ordinary hours carries no surcharge" → 0 | `rate_pct: "0"` | 0.00 | **bears** |
| surcharge_labour_figure | `parameter` — yes, tiers select 267.75 / 267.75 / 446.25 | tier 1; 2 `service_labour_charge` rows + 1 `service_parts_order_record` (multi-source: two distinct record families) | "the labour standing on the job" → 446.25 | `labour_base: "labour_all"` | RND(MX(446.25−40,0)×0.15,2) = **60.94** | **bears** |
| surcharge_base_restatement | `method` — yes, tiers change the algorithm (net of write-offs / restate at the service rate / as booked) | tier 1; goodwill write-off 40.00 on the job | "taken as it was booked" → `labour_base` | `net_base: "labour_base"` | RND(267.75×0.15,2) = **40.16** | **bears** |
| surcharge_day_anchor | `method` — yes, an anchor factor: the tiers change which record the day is read from | tier 1; `reschedule_count 1` + 2 labour rows | "the surcharge percent that applies to the day the surcharge is booked" → NOW | `rate_day: "NOW"` | 2026-09-18 is a Friday, window "morning" → `rate_pct = 0` → **0.00** | **bears** |

`baseline.rule` of this policy restates only the fall-throughs ("the labour standing on the job", "taken as it was
booked", "the day the surcharge is booked"), so no factor's ladder leaks into it. Counts: 4 factors, 2 `parameter`,
2 `method`, 1 multi-source, 0 cross-difficulty — inside the bounds.

**Computation 3 — `payment_amount` (4 factors; 2 `parameter`, 2 `method`).** Baseline result: `scope_total 429.91`,
`reliefs_recognised 0`, `payments_recognised 0`, `older_due 0` → **429.91** (definite, ≠ 303.43). Near-misses: the
`reschedule_fee` row whose `event_date` is 2026-08-31 while its `visit_date` is 2026-09-04 (it is excluded from

### verdict

- **Policy self-consistency: SOURCE-POLICY RED** — F-1 and F-2 (demonstrated below on this world).
- **Problem tree: SOURCE-CHAIN RED** — the tree itself holds and both edges bear weight, but two facts
  `prerequisite_closure` asserts about this world are false (F-10, F-11).
- **Factors bear weight: SOURCE-FACTOR RED** — all 14 bear weight, but F-4 (two of them rest on a baseline the
  policy's own `baseline.rule` contradicts) and F-6 (five sit on a `baseline.rule` sentence with no method).
- **Unique solution: PASS** — my blind derivation reproduces GT item by item, every parameter, owner, order and the
  terminal state; the closest alternatives are excluded by rule sentence + seeded row above.

## findings

**F-1 — SOURCE-POLICY RED. Undeclared override hands this task a second defensible surcharge.**
- Symptom: two clauses the KB publishes together give two different figures for `surcharge_amount` — 34.16 and
  40.16 — and only one of them is the scored value.
- Root cause: `service_ext_out_of_hours_surcharge` carries `overwrite: []` while its rule moves the surcharge base
  away from the chargeable labour base fixes. The deviation is an intermediate with no new parameter name
  (`net_base`), the "anonymous intermediate factor" form.
- Evidence: base, `service.extended.yaml` line ~975 (`service_appointment_scheduling.rule`): "Work outside the
  service's ordinary hours or at a weekend carries the service's surcharge **on the labour**, and the two surcharges
  are not both applied to the same hour." Base `service_labour_pricing.rule` + `formula`:
  "Chargeable labour is the hours actually worked … times the service's hourly rate";
  `round(max(minimum_labour_hours, labour_hours) * base_labour_rate_usd_per_hour, 2)`. Extended, same file,
  `service_ext_out_of_hours_surcharge.rule`: "where write-offs already stand on the job, **the write-offs recorded on
  it come off the labour before the surcharge is worked out**". Seeded rows: labour
  `912247e2-8b5a-431e-8c36-08b52105ab95` (`charge_amount 267.75`, 2.25 h @ 119.00, `visit_date 2026-09-12`) and
  write-off `894cac5a-3c17-442a-8861-11818afa258b` (`waiver_amount 40.0`, `waiver_reason goodwill`).
- Demonstrated consequence: the chargeable labour of the Saturday attendance is 267.75 under base's own formula;
  base's surcharge clause gives 267.75 × 15 / 100 = **40.16**. The extended policy gives
  (267.75 − 40.00) × 15 / 100 = **34.16**, which is gold. An agent that follows the base clause books 40.16, and the
  error propagates: the relief becomes RND((267.75 + 40.16) × 0.25, 2) + 11.00 = 87.98 and the settlement becomes
  MX(RND(462.91 + 35.00 − 127.98 − 62.00, 2), 0) = 307.93. All three scored figures move.
  GT's own `factor_sensitivity` records 40.16 as the `surcharge_base_restatement` baseline, i.e. the artifacts already
  compute the base-clause figure and treat it only as a wrong answer, without declaring the override that makes it
  wrong.
- Affected artifact and location: `env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/installation_service_desk/service.extended.yaml`,
  `extended_policies[0] service_ext_out_of_hours_surcharge` — `overwrite: []`, `rule` (the write-off and rate-restatement
  sentences), `compute.net_base`; scored parameters: `surcharge_amount`, and through it `waiver_amount` and
  `payment_amount`.
- Relation to previous revisions: first revision of this audit.

**F-2 — SOURCE-POLICY RED. The membership credit already spent is deducted twice.**
- Symptom: the relief sets 11.00 of benefit credit against the bill where the membership's own record shows 38.00 of
  unspent credit and the tier allows 50.00.
- Root cause: the extended rule first defines the credit as "the **unspent** benefit credit standing on the
  membership" and then holds back from it "what the membership year has already taken". `benefit_credit_balance` is
  by construction the granted credit less every redemption, so `spent_offset` subtracts a subset of the same
  redemptions a second time. Base `service_combo_plan_membership_interaction` says only "the membership's service
  benefit credit may then be spent against what is left", and the policy's declared `overwrite` names a different
  sentence (the discount-before-surcharge clause), so this deviation is undeclared.
- Evidence: `membership_holdings.0270f196-22e1-4ba8-b935-d1a95d64a99b.benefit_credit_balance = 38.0`, which is
  exactly the six seeded `membership_events` rows: grants 40.00 (2025-12-01) + 50.00 (2026-05-14) = 90.00, less
  redemptions 25.00 (2025-12-10) + 15.00 (2026-06-20) + 12.00 (2026-08-02) = 52.00. `compute.credit_spent_window =
  XSUM('membership','membership_events','benefit_amount', within_months=window_months,
  event_type='membership_benefit_redeem')` = 15.00 + 12.00 = 27.00 — two of the three redemptions already netted into
  the 38.00. `compute.credit_applied = MX(credit_available - spent_offset, 0)` = MX(38.00 − 27.00, 0) = 11.00.
- Demonstrated consequence: the same 27.00 is deducted twice. Base's clause gives a credit of 38.00 against what is
  left, so `waiver_amount` = 75.48 + 38.00 = **113.48**; the extended policy gives **86.48**. GT's own
  `factor_sensitivity` for `credit_spent_offset` records 113.48 as the baseline — the base-clause figure again
  recorded only as a wrong answer. No business writes off less than the credit its own ledger says is unspent.
- Affected artifact and location: same file, `extended_policies[1] service_ext_membership_service_relief` — `rule`
  ("From that credit is held back what the membership year has already taken"), `compute.spent_offset`,
  `compute.credit_applied`, factor `credit_spent_offset`, `overwrite` (which does not name this deviation); scored
  parameter `waiver_amount` and through it `payment_amount`.
- Relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**F-4 (this task's half) — SOURCE-FACTOR RED. Two factors rest on a baseline their own `baseline.rule` contradicts.**
- Symptom: a reader who has only the computation document lands on the *scored* tier value for
  `relief_labour_figure` and for `settlement_charge_scope`, so neither factor's own document can change any answer;
  and the figures the artifacts publish as those factors' baselines are not the figures the computation document
  yields.
- Root cause: charter-global — see `_difficulty.md` §`factor_ladders` F-4. `baseline.rule` restates the factor's
  entire three-tier ladder instead of its fall-through alone.
- Evidence, on this world:
  - `service_ext_membership_service_relief.baseline.rule` contains "where a payment has already been received on the
    job and the job carries labour for two or more attendances, the labour booked for the day the crew was last sent
    out is the figure taken". Payments 62.00 and 227.50 stand, and two labour rows stand, so that clause selects
    **267.75** — the scored `discount_base`. The factor declares `baseline: discount_base: "MX(labour_total -
    payments_total, 0)"` = MX(446.25 − 289.50, 0) = **156.75**, a figure the computation document never produces.
  - `service_ext_visit_settlement_payment.baseline.rule` contains "where a payment has already been received on the
    job and the job carries labour for two or more attendances, only the charges booked for the day the crew was last
    sent out are covered", which on this world selects **456.91** — the scored `scope_total`. The factor declares
    `baseline: scope_total: "MX(charges_total - payments_total, 0)"` = **429.91**.
- Demonstrated consequence: computing from `baseline.rule` alone gives the scored value for both inputs, which is the
  skill's own test for a decorative factor ("where that reading gives the scored value, the factor is decoration
  whatever `baseline` says"). It also makes `computations[2].baseline_result = 429.91` unreachable from the document
  that is supposed to produce it: the computation document as written gives 456.91 for the covered charges.
- Affected artifact and location: `service.extended.yaml` —
  `extended_policies[1].baseline.rule` vs `extended_policies[1].factors[1].baseline`;
  `extended_policies[2].baseline.rule` vs `extended_policies[2].factors[0].baseline`;
  `tasks/0.json computations[1].factor_sensitivity[1]` (58.73) and `computations[2].factor_sensitivity[0]` (276.43),
  `computations[2].baseline_result` (429.91).
- Relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**F-6 (this task's half) — SOURCE-FACTOR RED. The baselines of policies 2 and 3 are not self-sufficient.**
- Symptom: a reader of the computation document alone cannot reach a definite number for
  `payment_amount`, because the document subtracts and adds three quantities it never defines; the same for the
  relief's discount share.
- Root cause: charter-global — `_difficulty.md` §`factor_ladders` F-6.
- Evidence: `extended_policies[2].baseline.rule`: "the figure they settle is the charges the settlement covers,
  **plus the older charges standing unsettled that are due with them, less the relief already recognised on the job
  and less the money already held against those charges**" — and nothing else in `baseline.rule` says what any of the
  three is. `extended_policies[1].baseline.rule`: "and adds to it **the share** of the job's chargeable labour that
  the membership's own discount should have taken off" — the share is nowhere in `baseline.rule`.
- Demonstrated consequence on this world: three readings of the settlement's baseline document are all defensible and
  all different — 456.91 (take the three unstated terms as nothing, which is what the factors' fall-throughs say),
  456.91 + 35.00 − 126.48 − 289.50 = 75.93 (read "the older charges standing unsettled" as the 35.00 slot-move fee,
  "the relief already recognised" as the 126.48 of write-offs and "the money already held" as the 289.50 of payments
  on the record), and the declared 429.91. The document that must yield "a definite, wrong answer" yields at least
  three.
- Affected artifact and location: `service.extended.yaml` `extended_policies[1].baseline` and
  `extended_policies[2].baseline`; `tasks/0.json computations[1].baseline_result`, `computations[2].baseline_result`.
- Relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**F-10 — SOURCE-CHAIN RED. `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing` asserts a figure that is false on this world.**
- Symptom: the closure states that skipping the surcharge moves `payment_amount` from 303.43 to **269.27**. It moves
  it to **277.81**.
- Root cause: the figure was obtained by subtracting the skipped surcharge (34.16) from the gold settlement without
  re-deriving the relief on the skipped world — the closure's own previous clause records the relief falling from
  86.48 to 77.94, and that 8.54 has to come back into the settlement.
- Evidence and recomputation, on `initial_state` + a relief of 77.94 and no surcharge row:
  `charges_last_sent = 267.75 + 155.00 = 422.75`; `scope_total = 422.75` (tier 1 still: two payments, two labour
  rows); `waivers_total = 40.00 + 77.94 = 117.94`, `membership_waivers = 77.94 > 0` so
  `reliefs_recognised = 117.94`; `payments_recognised = 62.00`; `older_due = 35.00`;
  `result = MX(RND(422.75 + 35.00 − 117.94 − 62.00, 2), 0) = 277.81`. 303.43 − 34.16 + 8.54 = 277.81 confirms it
  arithmetically.
- Demonstrated consequence: the proof the artifact submits for this edge's weight is wrong by 8.54. The edge does bear
  weight (277.81 ≠ 303.43), so the *relationship* survives, but the closure's evidence for it does not, and the same
  false figure is repeated in `design_rationale` ("skipping the surcharge moves waiver_amount from 86.48 to 77.94 and
  payment_amount from 303.43 to 269.27") together with a false provenance claim ("the skip figures in
  edge_load_bearing … are the outputs of that same harness").
- Affected artifact and location: `tasks/0.json` `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[1].skipped_effect`, and
  `design_rationale`, PROBLEM-TREE CARD, "per-edge deletion sensitivity (actual figures)".
- Relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**F-11 — SOURCE-CHAIN RED. `prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness` asserts a terminal state the reversed order does
not produce.**
- Symptom: the closure argues the order is forced because "granting the relief first gives 77.94 and a settlement of
  311.97 that **leaves the job 8.54 out**, so no other order reproduces the terminal state". The reversed order
  clears the job to **0.00**, exactly as the gold order does.
- Root cause: the claim compares the reversed order's relief (77.94) with the gold relief (86.48) and reports the
  8.54 difference as a residue, without noticing that the settlement figure is itself recomputed on the reversed
  world and absorbs it.
- Evidence and recomputation, on `initial_state` + relief 77.94 + surcharge 34.16 (relief granted first):
  `charges_total = 719.41`; `scope_total = 456.91`; `reliefs_recognised = 117.94`; `payments_recognised = 62.00`;
  `older_due = 35.00`; `result = MX(RND(456.91 + 35.00 − 117.94 − 62.00, 2), 0) = 311.97` — which the closure gets
  right — and then outstanding = 719.41 − 289.50 − 117.94 − 311.97 = **0.00**.
- Demonstrated consequence: the stated ground for order-uniqueness does not hold. The order is nonetheless uniquely
  forced, by the prerequisite sentence "The relief is worked out only after the surcharge entry owed for the
  attendance it covers stands on the job's account", so this is a false assertion in a proof field rather than a
  second solution — but the terminal state is *not* what distinguishes the two orders, and any reader checking the
  closure's own argument will find it fails.
- Affected artifact and location: `tasks/0.json` `prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness`; repeated in
  `design_rationale`, PROBLEM-TREE CARD, "parallel edges: … the reversed order gives 77.94 and 311.97 and leaves the
  job 8.54 out".
- Relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**O-23 — observation. `design_rationale` names the wrong factors as multi-source.**
It asserts "Multi-source factors: service_credit_available and credit_spent_offset (each tier beyond the
fall-through combines the membership's standing or redemption count with a figure from its ledger or its tier)".
`service_credit_available`'s second tier is the bare single condition "no Circle membership stands active on the
profile", and `credit_spent_offset`'s first tier is the single comparison "the benefit redemptions booked on the
membership inside the window have reached the redemptions its tier allows in a year"; neither is a conjunction over
distinct records. The task does satisfy the floor — `surcharge_labour_figure` (labour rows ∧ a parts-order row),
`money_already_held` (a parts-order row ∧ a payment row), `older_charges_due` (a fee row ∧ the waiver rows) and
`labour_relief_share` (rework rows ∧ the agreement's `work_type`) each have every non-fall-through tier compound over
distinct records — so no consequence follows and this is not a red light; but the sentence asserts a structural fact
about the ladders that is false. Location: `tasks/0.json design_rationale`, FACTOR CARD, membership-relief block.

**O-5 / O-6 / O-8 / O-10 (charter-global, bearing on this task).** See `_difficulty.md` §`findings`. On this task:
the weekend surcharge is filed under `charge_kind="after_hours_surcharge"` (the only surcharge value the schema
carries, and the value policy 2 filters on, so no figure moves); `feeable_job_state` does not enumerate a surcharge
among its fee kinds although the job's `dispatched` status satisfies it anyway; `writeoff_service_charge_816a24da`
would accept `waiver_reason="contract_term"` just as readily as `membership_benefit`, so the state the settlement's
prerequisite sentence waits on is resolvable only from the policies' subject matter; and the write-off cap the
extended policy applies is the job's 389.91 rather than line L2's 416.91 (456.91 charged on L2 less the 40.00 already
written off there), which is tighter here and so changes nothing.

### revision_2 / re-derivation on the amended charter

I re-derived all three scored amounts and all fourteen sensitivity figures from the amended charter and this
unchanged world, before reading the new GT.

**Step 1 — `surcharge_amount`.** The only change in this policy's compute that touches any world is the
Saturday-evening guard in `rate_pct` (`attendance_dow > 0 **and attendance_dow < 6**`), which closes revision 1's
O-1. On this world `attendance_dow = DAYS('2026-01-04','2026-09-12') % 7 = 251 % 7 = 6` and
`scheduled_window = "morning"`, so the weekend branch is taken as before: `labour_base = 267.75`,
`net_base = MX(267.75 - 40.00, 0) = 227.75`, `rate_pct = 15`, `result = RND(227.75 × 15 / 100, 2) = **34.16**`.
Unchanged, correctly.

**Step 2 — `waiver_amount`, the F-2 fix.** The old `credit_applied = MX(credit_available - spent_offset, 0)` is
gone; the new construction is `credit_applied = MN(credit_available, year_allowance)` with
`year_allowance` a separate ladder. On this world:
`discount_base = 267.75`, `surcharge_scope = 34.16`, `relief_rate = 25`,
`discount_owed = RND((267.75 + 34.16) × 25 / 100, 2) = 75.48`;
`credit_available = 38.00` (active, and 38.00 below the tier's 50.00);

`credit_spent_window = 27.00` (15.00 on 2026-06-20 and 12.00 on 2026-08-02; the 25.00 of 2025-12-10 is 9 months

`result = MN(RND(75.48 + 23.00, 2), 389.91) = **98.48**` (was 86.48).

**The F-2 fix is genuine, not a rewording.** I checked the double deduction directly. The membership's purse,

Revision 1 then subtracted 27.00 of those same 52.00 from it again (38.00 − 27.00 = 11.00). Revision 2 leaves the

never from the purse; 23.00 binds because it is below the purse. The base clause the deviation rests on
("and the membership's service benefit credit may then be spent against what is left") is now declared superseded,
and the replacement carries the no-double-deduction rule in words: "so no redemption already netted out of the
membership's own balance is deducted from that balance a second time." **F-2 closed.**

**The customer's request still pins that figure exactly.** Outstanding after both prerequisite writes is

## findings — revision_2

**F-16 — SOURCE-CHAIN RED. `edge_load_bearing[0]` still asserts a residue this world does not produce.**
- Symptom: the closure states that skipping the relief leaves "the job … 98.48 out instead of clearing to nothing".
  Skipping the relief and settling the 389.91 the policy then produces clears the job to **0.00**.
- Root cause: the residue is taken as the missing write-off (98.48) rather than recomputed from the ledger after
  the alternative settlement has been applied — the same mechanism as revision 1's F-11 and F-13, which were fixed
  in `order_uniqueness` but not here.
- Evidence and recomputation: charges after the surcharge write are 178.50 + 49.00 + 35.00 + 267.75 + 155.00 +
  34.16 = 719.41; payments are 62.00 + 227.50 + 389.91 = 679.41; write-offs are the 40.00 goodwill row alone;
  719.41 − 679.41 − 40.00 = **0.00**. The reason is structural, not arithmetic luck: on the skipped world the
  settlement figure *is* the outstanding figure (456.91 + 35.00 − 40.00 − 62.00 = 389.91 = 719.41 − 289.50 −
  40.00), so settling it always clears the job.
- Demonstrated consequence: the proof the artifact offers for this edge's weight rests on a false fact. The edge
  does bear weight (389.91 ≠ 291.43), so the relationship survives, but the closure's stated evidence does not, and
  a reader checking it will find the opposite of what it claims.
- Affected artifact and location: `tasks/0.json` `prerequisite_closure.edge_load_bearing[0].skipped_effect`. The
  same clause is **not** repeated in `design_rationale`, which states only the correct
  "skipping the relief moves payment_amount from 291.43 to 389.91".
- Relation to previous revisions: **present in revision 1 in the same form** ("the job is left with 86.48 still
  outstanding instead of clearing to nothing", likewise false — that world also clears to 0.00) and **not caught by
  me then**. Revision 1's `source_gt_comparison` compared the 389.91 and marked the row "same" without checking the
  residue clause beside it. Recorded here as my own miss, not as a new regression by the reworker.

**F-17, F-18 — SOURCE-FACTOR RED (charter-global findings, demonstrated on this world).** Stated once in
`env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/audits/policy_task/installation_service_desk/_difficulty.md`
§`revision_2 / new charter-global findings`. F-17 is a regression against revision 1's pass on
`service_credit_available`; F-18 is new in the factor that replaced `credit_spent_offset`.

**O-24, O-26, O-28, O-30, O-31 — observations bearing on this task.** O-24, O-26, O-30 and O-31 are stated in
`_difficulty.md` §revision_2. One is specific to this task's persona:

**O-28 — observation. A persona line states a world fact the seed contradicts, on the quantity that now decides
the answer.** `user_scenario`: "if she is asked how much credit her membership has she says she has no idea,
**she has never spent it**, and leaves it to him to look up." The seeded ledger carries three
`membership_benefit_redeem` rows totalling 52.00, of which the 27.00 inside the four-month window is now the
quantity that fixes `year_allowance` at 23.00 and so decides the scored 98.48. Because she defers to the record in
the same breath and the record is the authoritative source, an agent reading the ledger is not misled and GT
remains uniquely derivable, so this is not a persona/DB conflict on a fact the agent must resolve. Present in
revision 1 and not caught then; it matters more now than it did, because revision 1's arithmetic also turned on the
27.00 but the line was one step further from the scored figure.
